run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T04:20:34Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a burst of HTTP 500 responses on POST /api/checkout that frontend-proxy proxied from the 'frontend' service between roughly 04:11:00Z and 04:12:43.874Z on 2026-11-15. The deepest cause the evidence supports is the rolling replacement of the single payment replica: Deployment payment scaled up ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 (0 to 1) at 04:10:56Z and killed the old pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 at 04:10:59Z, but the new payment container (Started 04:10:59Z, Pod Ready=True from 04:10:59Z) logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' only at 04:12:14.571Z, and the payment Deployment container spec has no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe. During that gap checkout's client spans oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR while payment's own server spans grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge showed no error status and almost no traffic, i.e. the failing RPCs never reached a listening payment server. Errors propagated one step at a time: checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, then frontend POST /api/checkout (HTTP 500), then frontend-proxy ingress ERROR spans (rate identical to its CLIENT span 'router frontend egress'), which is the series the alert is about. Everything was back to normal by about 04:12:43.9Z; payment is healthy now (Running, 0 restarts, charges completing, no ERROR span series).

claims.text: In the incident window, service_name=frontend-proxy has only two span operations, 'ingress' (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and 'router frontend egress' (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT), and traces_span_metrics_calls_total exists only with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET for them.

frontend-proxy error spans: rate of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} rose from a background of 0 to 0.0148 per second to 0.2556/s (evaluation 04:13:34) and 0.2593/s (04:15:34), while the UNSET (total) ingress rate stayed flat at about 9.8-10.1 per second; the CLIENT span 'router frontend egress' ERROR rate was exactly the same 0.2556/s at those evaluations, i.e. about 2.5% of ingress spans errored, all at the egress step.

Across all services, the only error-status span series with a real spike in this period were on the checkout to payment path: checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 0.1793/s and 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' 0.1793/s (04:13:34), frontend 'POST' 0.2556/s, 'POST /api/checkout' 0.2556/s, 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 0.2556/s and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 0.2556/s, frontend-proxy 'ingress' 0.2556/s and 'router frontend egress' 0.2556/s. The only other nonzero error series were low-rate flagd EventStream noise (about 0.0037/s) on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation, present intermittently before and after the burst.

At 30-second resolution, checkout's client span 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' ERROR rate was 0.4789/s at evaluation 04:12:30 and 0.4556/s at 04:13:00, 04:13:30 and 04:14:00, and 0 by 04:14:30; at 04:13:30 the same span's STATUS_CODE_UNSET rate was 0 while 'POST /api/checkout' had ERROR 0.4556/s and UNSET 0, i.e. essentially every checkout request in that interval failed at the Charge call.

frontend-proxy logged 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream' repeatedly: within 04:11:00-04:12:40 there were 64 such matching lines (the 40 newest span 04:11:42.119Z to 04:12:39.900Z and 24 earlier ones were omitted by the limit), plus 5 more up to 04:12:43.874Z, and none between 04:12:43.9Z and 04:15:00Z. The 500 was returned by the upstream 'frontend' service (via_upstream, 21-byte response body), not generated by the proxy.

checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-h9bvp logged normal successful checkout flows again from 04:13:18Z ('[PlaceOrder]', 'payment went through', 'order placed', 'order confirmation email sent'), confirming recovery right after the burst.

Kubernetes state: pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d started 2026-11-15T04:10:56Z with 0 restarts and was Ready=True from 04:10:59Z, while every other otel-demo pod listed started 03:38-03:40Z; it is the only pod in the namespace younger than the incident.

The payment replacement was performed by its own Deployment: events show Deployment payment 'Scaled up replica set payment-54499f9786 from 0 to 1' at 04:10:56Z, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate of payment-54499f9786-4r25d, pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started at 04:10:56-04:10:59Z, then Killing of the old pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 and Deployment 'Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0' at 04:10:59Z. Both ReplicaSets are owned by Deployment payment and specify the same image string ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, and the old ReplicaSet now has 0 replicas.

Deployment payment (replicas 1, RollingUpdate maxSurge 25% maxUnavailable 25%) defines container 'payment' with containerPort 8080 and no readinessProbe, no livenessProbe and no startupProbe, so the pod is declared ready as soon as the container process starts.

payment container logs show 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' only at 2026-11-15T04:12:14.571Z, about 75 seconds after the container started at 04:10:59Z, and the first 'Charge request received.' at 04:12:47.971Z; therefore from 04:10:59Z (old pod killed) until 04:12:14Z the payment workload had no listening gRPC server.

payment's own server-side span 'grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' has no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series at all in the window and its UNSET rate dropped to 0.0667/s (04:12:30, 04:13:00) and 0 (04:13:30, 04:14:00) before returning to 0.75/s at 04:14:30, while checkout's client 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' was reporting errors in the same interval: the failed calls did not reach a payment server span.

Root cause: the payment Deployment rollout (new ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 at 04:10:56Z, old pod killed 04:10:59Z) combined with the absence of any readiness or startup probe on the payment container meant the new pod was marked Ready at 04:10:59Z and received Service traffic while its gRPC server was not listening until 04:12:14Z. Checkout's Charge RPCs failed during that gap, PlaceOrder errored, frontend returned HTTP 500 on /api/checkout, and frontend-proxy's ingress spans (mirroring its 'router frontend egress' client spans) turned to STATUS_CODE_ERROR, which is what the RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy reports.

Alert timing versus the burst: the observed 500 burst ended at 04:12:43.874Z, about 8 minutes before the alert start time 04:20:34Z, and the metric views' data_as_of is 474-485 seconds older than their observed_at (for example data_as_of 04:29:34Z read at 04:37:28Z). The alert may therefore have been evaluated over lagged telemetry covering the burst; the alert's own expression, labels and evaluation window could not be checked because this Prometheus returned no rules.

Magnitude consistency: the alert annotation value 0.0222 (2.22%) is close to the measured peak ratio at frontend-proxy during the burst, 0.2556 error spans/s out of about 10.15 ingress spans/s (about 2.5%); this is a similarity of magnitude only and does not prove the rule's denominator or window.

payment is not in a failed state now: pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d is Running and Ready with 0 restarts and an empty lastState; its logs from about 04:23Z to 04:24Z contain many 'Charge request received.' and 'Transaction complete.' pairs; and no payment span series carries STATUS_CODE_ERROR. The failure was a short unavailability window, not a persistent payment fault.

Rejected: frontend-proxy is itself the faulty component. Its ingress ERROR rate equals its own client-side 'router frontend egress' ERROR rate exactly (0.2556/s at both evaluations, so every ERROR ingress span is matched by a failed upstream call), and the 500 responses it logged were produced upstream by 'frontend' (via_upstream), so the proxy is reporting a downstream failure rather than causing it.

Rejected: another checkout dependency caused the PlaceOrder failures. In the all-services error breakdown the only error series on the checkout path were 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' and 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' at identical rates (0.1793/s), i.e. the failure was at the Charge step; the flagd EventStream errors on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation are low-rate background present before and after the burst and their about 0.0037/s rates are far below the burst.

Rejected: the payment pod was damaged (Evicted, OOMKilled or crashed). It has 0 restarts and an empty lastState, there is no Evicted, OOMKilled or Unhealthy event, and the replacement is recorded as its own Deployment and ReplicaSet actions (ScalingReplicaSet, SuccessfulCreate, SuccessfulDelete) with the same image string, i.e. a rollout rather than damage.

Add a readinessProbe (and preferably a startupProbe) to the payment container gating on the gRPC port 8080, or otherwise gate readiness on the gRPC server being up. With such a probe the RollingUpdate (maxUnavailable 25% rounds to 0 for 1 replica) would keep the old ready pod until the new one actually serves, removing the about 75-second gap observed between 04:10:59Z and 04:12:14Z.

Investigate why the payment container needed about 75 seconds (04:10:59Z Started to 04:12:14.571Z gRPC server started) before listening even though the container image was already present on the node, and audit the other otel-demo Deployments for the same missing readiness probes.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules returned status no_data with empty content both unfiltered (6233a11f-0550-4f9e-a504-51e11486f7af-t0) and with rule_name=RequestErrorRate (718c5fb1-bc18-4c14-9b8a-d4956bc7a13b-t0), so the alert expression, window and evaluation time are unknown and the annotation value 0.0222 at 04:20:34Z could not be reproduced from the available series.

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend-proxy in 04:10-04:16Z, 04:25-04:37Z and no error=true traces for frontend-proxy or checkout (011c5406-9fa3-4074-9451-6dc79879352c-t0, 9a237674-0450-4e61-a695-d3c2c057d1be-t0, 9cf51585-a706-4778-8877-d862ecedad3c-t1, 7e9983e1-ab1e-4502-ab0f-17374cd940ab-t0 all no_data) although traces_list_services lists frontend-proxy, so no span-level error detail or gRPC status text for the failed Charge calls could be read.

Metric queries for rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count (9a04072c-0259-4363-9142-cee6643f99f3-t0) and for kube_pod_* metric names (69f45b89-7883-4539-9147-5c9a8cef187a-t1) returned no_data, so gRPC status-code breakdowns and kube-state pod object history are unavailable; kube_pod_container_info could not be queried (d051994e-6727-4e5a-b512-065412f85205-t1 no_data), so image digests were not comparable beyond the identical image string.
The old payment pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 no longer exists and its logs are unavailable ('previous terminated container not found'), so its shutdown behaviour at 04:10:59Z is unknown.

frontend logs returned zero bytes and status no_data for 04:10-04:13:30 (69f45b89-7883-4539-9147-5c9a8cef187a-t0), so the frontend-side error text for the HTTP 500 responses is unknown; the 500s are evidenced only from frontend-proxy's access log.

Two log views hit limits and are incomplete: frontend-proxy 04:11:00-04:12:40 showed the newest 40 of 64 matching lines (45a435e1-40c0-440b-909d-80d3e05a620e-t0) and the 04:05-04:11 read reached the 4 MiB limit with status no_data (848efcca-47ab-488d-b335-e3087f562855-t1), so 500 lines before 04:11:00 were not read; frontend-proxy 04:10-04:13:30 (f6984443-e1ca-4e35-a7de-da4da04a0907-t0) and checkout 04:11:30-04:13:30 (98b05a48-6db4-4887-8fa5-ce74798458c1-t1) were also limited to the newest lines shown.
What triggered the payment rolling update (a pod-template change) is unknown: the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

Other otel-demo services (cart, currency, email, image-provider, product-catalog, quote, shipping) have no STATUS_CODE_ERROR span series in this window at all; a missing series is unknown rather than proof they were error-free, so no health clearance is claimed for them.
Kubernetes objects were read after the incident (observed_at about 04:37-04:38Z) and events cover only their own timestamps, so earlier object states are not proven (the views state this limitation).
next_steps: Pull the RequestErrorRate rule definition and its evaluation history from the Prometheus and Alertmanager that actually evaluate it, to confirm the window and denominator behind the 0.0222 reading at 04:20:34Z.

Retrieve span-level exemplars or collector trace data for 04:10:59-04:12:45Z to capture the exact gRPC status returned to checkout on oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (expected an UNAVAILABLE or connection-refused class failure).
Add readiness and startup probes to the payment deployment, audit the other otel-demo deployments for the same gap, and re-verify that a rolling update no longer drops endpoints.
Check cluster and change records for whatever edited the payment pod template at 04:10:56Z, and consider gating config-only rollouts of single-replica services.
